nodes.title: Card — kanban metadata + column-transition policy
nodes.description: The Card bounded context. Owns the kanban entity that represents one unit of work, its column lifecycle, and the cross-aggregate policy that drives Workspace state when a column changes.

nodes.title: Household — registered project bundle (meta-repo + manifest + repos)
nodes.description: The Household bounded context. Manages the named project bundles Reeve operates on — a meta-repo with a household.json manifest declaring sibling repos and a knowledge base. Implements HouseholdLookup for Card.

nodes.title: Workspace — per-card materialization (clones + container + listener)
nodes.description: The Workspace bounded context. Provisions a per-card on-disk working tree (poly-repo clones via --reference --dissociate), spawns and tears down the devcontainer that hosts the agent, and runs the background fetch worker that mirrors card-branch refs into the host meta-repo.

nodes.title: Async-over-sync — spawn_blocking + blocking_lock around rusqlite
nodes.description: How Reeve's Sqlite*Repo adapters expose async traits while using synchronous rusqlite under the hood. The spawn_blocking + blocking_lock pattern lives inside the adapter; consumers never see it. Avoids holding locks across .await points.

nodes.title: γ type pattern — domain entity + wire DTO + From/TryFrom boundary
nodes.description: How Reeve bridges a typed domain entity (private fields, invariants enforced at construction) with a serde-derived wire DTO. From in one direction always succeeds; TryFrom in the other direction re-runs invariants. Validation lives at the boundary; once you hold the domain type, it's known-valid.

nodes.title: Inverted-dependency ports — the consumer crate defines the trait
nodes.description: Cross-crate dependency direction is architecturally significant. Reeve places port traits in the consumer crate; supplier crates depend on the consumer and implement the trait. The Dependency Inversion Principle in Cargo.toml form.

nodes.title: Repository pattern — port + pub(crate) adapter + factory function
nodes.description: How Reeve structures persistence (and other "side effects") within a bounded-context crate. A public trait defines the port; a pub(crate) struct implements it for SQLite; a pub factory returns an Arc<dyn Trait>. Callers never name the concrete type.

nodes.title: Architecture — vertical-slice bounded contexts with inverted-dependency ports
nodes.description: The high-level rules every Reeve change must follow. Six crates, one bounded context per crate (except reeved which composes them), inverted-dependency ports between contexts, pub(crate) adapters with factory functions, schema independence, CI lint to enforce facade discipline.

nodes.title: Commit and PR conventions
nodes.description: How Reeve commits look, why they're shaped that way, and the conventions agents and humans follow. Imperative mood, conventional-commit prefixes with milestone numbers, heredoc body for non-trivial commits, Co-Authored-By trailers for agent work.

nodes.title: Testing strategy
nodes.description: How Reeve tests are organised. Per-crate unit tests with in-memory SQLite and mock ports. Cross-crate integration tests in the tests/ crate. Docker-gated e2e tests for the full container lifecycle. Drift protection for the wire/domain γ boundary.

nodes.title: Visibility modifiers — pub, pub(crate), pub(super), pub(in path)
nodes.description: How Reeve uses Rust's visibility modifiers to enforce architectural rules at compile time. pub for crate API; pub(crate) for adapters that should be unnameable outside the crate; pub(super) and pub(in path) for tighter scoping inside a crate.
